title: Room-Temperature Supersolid in an Exciton-Polariton Condensate: Order Chosen by Spontaneous Symmetry Breaking

claims.claim: A new type of optical microcavity, filled with a nematic liquid crystal and two layers of the organic polymer MeLPPP, achieves supersolidity of a quantum fluid of light at room temperature
Exciton-polaritons condense in two degenerate minima of the dispersion created by liquid-crystal-induced Rashba-Dresselhaus spin-orbit coupling

Density stripes appear at random positions from one condensate realisation to the next despite a random disorder potential, showing immunity to disorder and spontaneous breaking of translational invariance
claims.evidence: Paper abstract; press: fringes land in different positions with each laser pulse

claims.claim: Vortices appear at random, another feature of superfluids
Two forms of order appear at the same time, one in polarisation and one in light intensity; the state is electrically tunable

key_numbers.sample_usable_time: a few hours after assembly (organic semiconductor reacts with the liquid crystal)

key_quotes.speaker: Guillaume Malpuech, Institut Pascal (CNRS)
key_quotes.quote: This is a textbook example of spontaneous symmetry breaking. Theory predicted that the supersolid could choose among several equivalent states, and that is exactly what we observed.

key_quotes.speaker: Wiktor Piecek, Military University of Technology
key_quotes.quote: Our liquid-crystal microcavities can operate even at temperatures approaching 60°C

assembly_theory_relevance.status: interpretation by the repository author; not a claim made by the paper
assembly_theory_relevance.order_by_symmetry_breaking: The rules of the system allow many equivalent stripe positions. Each laser pulse, the condensate picks one, and disorder in the sample does not pin the choice. Structure emerges as a choice among equivalent states, which is the kind of contingent, historical ordering assembly theory cares about.
assembly_theory_relevance.layered_order: Two orders at once (polarisation and intensity) is a small example of nested structure in a light-matter system
assembly_theory_relevance.polariton_bridge_to_BIO-006: Both studies are about polaritons, light-matter hybrids that persist at room or body temperature: the mito-polariton proposed at 71 THz in living mitochondria, and the exciton-polariton supersolid here. In both, the effect needs a carefully structured cavity: cristae of the right length in one, an engineered liquid-crystal microcavity in the other.
assembly_theory_relevance.important_difference: This entry is a directly observed, peer-reviewed condensate in an engineered, laser-pumped device. The mitochondrial polariton is a model-based interpretation in an unreplicated preprint, with no condensate and no supersolid. This entry does not show that anything similar happens in cells.
assembly_theory_relevance.open_question: Could an assembly-style measure of the stripe pattern (how many steps to build it, how it varies pulse to pulse) separate genuine symmetry-breaking order from disorder-pinned patterns?

limitations: Photonics, not biology: it says nothing directly about living systems
Single study; not yet independently replicated
Polaritons last only picoseconds and need laser excitation
Samples degrade within hours because the organic semiconductor reacts with the liquid crystal, so each repeat needs a new sample
Electrical tunability and the two simultaneous orders are reported in press coverage; check the full paper before relying on details
next_experiments: A material pairing that does not degrade, so the same sample can be measured repeatedly
Map how the stripe period and order change with applied voltage
Statistics of stripe positions over many pulses, to quantify how random the choice is

cross_references.relation: Mitochondrial polariton (71 THz), bioRxiv preprint: a proposed light-matter hybrid in living cells
Quantum Fluid Crystallization / Frozen Light: polariton condensates with solid-like order; this entry is a 2026 room-temperature, peer-reviewed example
Coupling-Induced Order: strong matter-field coupling produces ordered configurations

integration.cluster_1_quantum_foundations: A macroscopic quantum state (condensate, superfluid, supersolid) at room temperature rather than near absolute zero
integration.cluster_4_complexity_science: Order that emerges through spontaneous symmetry breaking and resists disorder
integration.cluster_5_topological_systems: Spin-orbit coupled condensate with randomly appearing vortices
